title: CheckResult@1 payload
description: One execution of one check, recorded per attempt. Each execution is its own immutable artifact, so a later run never erases an earlier one and 'the checks were green' always names the execution it describes. Two distinct shapes exist: a local result records the command that ran; a remote result (ADR-0136) carries `remote`, the `af/RemoteCheckEvidence@1` artifact its status derives from, and no program, exit code, arguments or `stderr`; its `stdout`, present only when the check did not pass, is the bounded log excerpt of the remote jobs that did not succeed. A mixture of the two is refused.

name.description: The check's identity within its pipeline.

status.description: `not_run` is the load-bearing one: a check that could not execute — missing program, unreachable host, a selector matching nothing — is NOT a pass, and must be representable as its own outcome rather than collapsing into failure or, worse, into silence.

exit_code.description: Absent exactly when the check never ran, and always on a remote result.

reason.description: Why a `not_run` check could not execute. Required for that status; a check that did not run without a stated reason is indistinguishable from one nobody defined. A remote result's reason begins with its evidence's reason code.

program.description: The executable, always a trusted literal from project configuration and never derived from anything under review. Absent only when the check named no program at all — a malformed definition has nothing to record here, and an empty string would claim it did — and on a remote result.

args.description: The rendered argument vector, each slot carrying its provenance. Kept in the record so a reviewer of the review can see exactly what ran, including which values came from untrusted input. Empty on a remote result.

required.description: Whether the gate blocks on this check. A required check that is `failed` or `not_run` fails the gate.

remote.description: The `af/RemoteCheckEvidence@1` artifact a remote executor's result derives from (ADR-0136). Present only on a remote result.

provenance.description: `literal` comes from trusted configuration and may be an option. `untrusted` is derived from the change under review — a path from the diff, a selector from a reviewer — and can never occupy an option position, whatever it looks like.
